author: Chapel Fowler
title: Former Clemson safety drawing rave reviews at SEC school. Why'd he transfer? - NewsBreak
text:
By Chapel Fowler ,
16 hours ago Former Clemson safety Khalil Barnes (7) transferred to Georgia this offseason Tony Walsh/Tony Walsh/UGAAA The baby picture said it all.
When former Clemson safety Khalil Barnes committed to Georgia out of the transfer portal in January, he didn’t need a slick social media edit. He just teed up an old photo of himself wearing a red and black UGA crewneck as a toddler.
“ New Profile Pic ,” Barnes wrote in a post on X.
For Barnes, an Athens native who grew up attending UGA games at Sanford Stadium and starred at nearby North Oconee High School , it was a special homecoming.
According to UGA coach Kirby Smart , it was also a partnership that should’ve started a lot sooner, if it wasn’t for some recruiting missteps by his program.
“He’s a kid that grew up in the shadows of our stadium,” Smart said of Barnes at SEC Media Days. “I’ve known his dad for a long time, back to when I was a player, and we probably messed it up when he was coming out. Didn’t do a good job.”
Georgia’s loss was Clemson’s gain. After signing with Dabo Swinney and the Tigers, Barnes — a late bloomer who’d initially committed to Wake Forest — put together a Freshman All-American season and was a regular starter from 2023-25.
Four years later, Clemson’s loss appears to Georgia’s gain.
Barnes, a senior, was recently named to the preseason All-SEC third team and is trending toward a starting role for the preseason No. 3 Bulldogs , who’ve won back-to-back SEC championships and should contend for a national title.
“We’re excited for the opportunity to take a kid home that played in a very good defensive system and that we’re excited to watch play for us,” Smart said.
But if Barnes was so good, why’d he leave Clemson?
Clemson safety Khalil Barnes (7) playing against South Carolina in 2024 Joshua Boucher/jboucher@thestate.com Recapping Khalil Barnes’ Clemson career, transfer decision Barnes was lights out to start his Clemson career, racking up Freshman All-American honors in 2023 and picking off four passes as a sophomore in 2024.
He had the most interceptions of any Clemson player in their first two seasons (seven) since Rashard Hall’s eight in 2009-10 , and he memorably recorded takeaways on back-to-back snaps in a road win against rival South Carolina in 2023.
In 2025, though, Barnes missed two games with injury and finished his junior year with no interceptions, forced fumbles or fumble recoveries.
He was also criticized online by some for what some perceived as a lack of hustle during a touchdown play against SMU, as well as a viral video during Clemson’s loss to Duke in which Barnes appeared to be looking away from Swinney as he lit into his defense in a passionate sideline rant after they allowed another long touchdown.
Barnes’ father, Ken, pushed back against some fans assertions’ about those video clips in posts on X, saying that they didn’t capture the full context .
It’s worth noting Barnes was far from the only Clemson player who saw a statistical drop-off last year. Cade Klubnik , Peter Woods and T.J. Parker were among other Tigers who didn’t fully deliver on their preseason expectations.
Every player in the Tigers’ secondary also had their fair share of coverage busts and mistakes as they struggled to get on the same page in new defensive coordinator Tom Allen’s system and Clemson finished 7-6 and 4-4 in the ACC.
It’s fair to say Barnes didn’t play to his full potential in 2025. It’s also fair to say Clemson, which fired longtime safeties coach Mickey Conn this offseason, didn’t provide the perfect environment for Barnes to do that as a junior.
A fresh start made some sense for both sides. Still, Swinney said in December after Barnes announced his plans to transfer, Clemson had wanted to keep him.
“Certainly didn’t want to (lose him),” Swinney said. “Listen, you’re gonna always have transfers in today’s world. I don’t know if there’ll be a team without one.”
Clemson coach Dabo Swinney (right) celebrates with safety Khalil Barnes (36) after Barnes’ interception against South Carolina in 2023. Jeff Blake/USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con UGA’s Smart: ‘We had to find a starter’ The Barnes-Clemson split may end up working out for both sides.
Clemson, which lost Barnes and fellow starting safety Ricardo Jones to the portal, signed transfer safeties Jerome Carter III (Old Dominion) and Corey Myrick (Southern Miss). Both players are proven veterans and likely Game 1 starters.
Meanwhile, Barnes is the favorite to start for Georgia at STAR, a hybrid linebacker/safety role that’s a key part of the Bulldogs’ defensive success.
Smart said Barnes’ experience and versatility were the top reasons Georgia pursued him. Barnes (6-0, 200) appeared in 37 games with 30 starts for Clemson and has played almost 2,000 snaps. 247Sports ranked him as the No. 12 safety in the portal .
“When we went in there, we had to find a starter,” Smart said. “... We had some good young players up and coming, but we needed a veteran.”
“Khalil fits in pretty well,” UGA linebacker Raylen Wilson added. “He likes to work.”
As Barnes prepares for his first season at Georgia, there’s no bad blood with his former school, which is just 90 minutes up the road from him in Athens.
Smart said Clemson’s coaches spoke highly of Barnes when he called them to vet Barnes as a transfer option. When he transferred, Barnes also publicly thanked Swinney for taking a chance on him as a three-star high school recruit and praised Clemson’s football program at large, as well as his former teammates.
“ I gave everything I had for y’all and the Paw,” Barnes wrote.
The State’s Jordan Kaye and Michael Sauls contributed reporting.
